decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY covering both interboard inputs, all external module connectors, and the total connector count.
The source specifies connectors on the existing sensor board and does not change the number or separation of project boards.
The candidate already has a complete same-message INTRODUCE for the SPS30 connector, cable compatibility, supply, I2C signals, SEL connection, and ground.
The sensor-board connector specification does not alter power-board battery access, connector orientation, placement, or mounting-hole clearance.
The source does not change the power board's dimensions, installation orientation, USB-C placement, aspect ratio, or mounting arrangement.
The six-pin signal connector described by the source is the main-to-sensor interface; it does not replace or modify the separate J_PWR_SIGNAL USB D+/D- route.
The source concerns sensor-board interboard and module connectors, not the three-pin battery connector or its unresolved pin order.
The source does not change the charge-status display method, dedicated charge LED connector, CHGLED circuit, or resistor population.
Specifying the sensor-board power connector pinout does not change the monitored rails, INA3221 selection, monitor position, measurement coverage, or spare channel count.
The source lists sensor-board connectors but makes no decision about LED supply voltage, data GPIO, level shifting, or standby power control.
Assigning SDA0/SCL0 and SDA1/SCL1 to sensor-board connectors does not change cable length, bus speed, pull-ups, or series-resistor conditioning.

The sensor-board power input pinout is compatible with the existing downstream 3.3V supply state and does not change the USB auxiliary regulator, source selection, powered load set, or standalone programming behavior.
